themes_detail.label: Street Condition Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints spiked to 141 THIS WEEK, a 286% increase versus the 8-week baseline of 36.5 weekly complaints (z-score: 8.1), indicating a sudden deterioration in road quality across Ridgewood/Glendale/Middle Village.
evidence: 141 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 36.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (286% spike)
Z-score of 8.1 indicates statistically significant anomaly
Snow/ice complaints (1,698 over 90 days) suggest winter weather may be compounding issue
Street condition appears in recurring CB budget requests, signaling chronic underinvestment
reporting_angles: Ground-level reporting: Which specific streets are deteriorating most? Are potholes, cracking, or flooding the primary complaints?
City response: Why the sudden spike this week? Has NYCDOT deployed resources or is this weather-related?
Chronic neglect angle: Why does CB repeatedly request street repairs if baseline complaints are already high?

themes_detail.label: Food Safety Red Flag
themes_detail.summary: Food establishment complaints jumped to 7 THIS WEEK, a 367% spike versus the 8-week baseline of 1.5 weekly complaints (z-score: 5.5), suggesting potential health code violations or inspector activity surge in local restaurants.
evidence: 7 food establishment complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (367% increase)
Z-score of 5.5 indicates highly anomalous spike
No recent Reddit or news coverage to explain sudden surge
Could indicate increased DOHMH inspection activity or genuine food safety cluster
reporting_angles: What specific restaurants or food establishments are generating complaints? Are violations concentrated in one neighborhood pocket?
Is DOHMH conducting a targeted inspection campaign, or is this reactive to complaints?
Interview local restaurant owners: Are they seeing increased enforcement, and is it fair?

themes_detail.label: Hazardous Materials Spike
themes_detail.summary: Hazardous materials complaints surged to 3 LAST WEEK, a 2,300% increase versus the 8-week baseline of 0.1 weekly complaints (z-score: 8.69), raising environmental and public health concerns in the district.
evidence: 3 hazardous materials complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (2,300% spike)
Z-score of 8.69 indicates extreme statistical anomaly
Coincides with spike in illegal dumping (37 complaints last week, up 185%)
372 building permits filed in last 90 days (283 alterations) could indicate construction-related hazmat exposure
reporting_angles: What materials were reported? Are complaints concentrated near construction sites or industrial areas?
Is there a connection between the 185% surge in illegal dumping and hazmat complaints? Are residents encountering dumped toxic materials?
Has NYCDEP or NYPD investigated any of the complaints? What follow-up occurred?

themes_detail.label: Illegal Dumping Surge
themes_detail.summary: Illegal dumping complaints jumped to 37 LAST WEEK, a 185% increase versus the 8-week baseline of 13.0 weekly complaints (z-score: 5.62), indicating a sudden surge in environmental violations that may be connected to the concurrent hazmat spike.
evidence: 37 illegal dumping complaints LAST WEEK vs. 13.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (185% increase)
Z-score of 5.62 indicates significant anomaly
Converges with hazmat spike (3 complaints last week) suggesting possible cross-contamination issue
Illegal parking remains district's chronic problem (6,138 over 90 days), suggesting limited enforcement capacity
reporting_angles: Where are dumping sites concentrated? Are they near highways, industrial zones, or residential streets?
Who is dumping and why the sudden spike? Interview Sanitation or environmental enforcement about enforcement patterns.
Is this connected to construction activity (372 permits filed) or external dumping rings?

themes_detail.label: Sanitation Worker Complaints
themes_detail.summary: Complaints about sanitation workers or vehicles jumped to 6 LAST WEEK, an 1,100% increase versus the 8-week baseline of 0.5 weekly complaints (z-score: 11.0), suggesting potential service failures or worker conduct issues in waste collection.
evidence: 6 sanitation worker/vehicle complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1,100% spike)
Z-score of 11.0 indicates extreme anomaly
Litter basket complaints also spiked (3 complaints 3 weeks ago, up 2,300%), suggesting sanitation system breakdown
No Reddit or news context explaining the sudden surge
reporting_angles: What specific complaints did residents file? Vehicle damage, route failures, worker conduct, or collection delays?
Is there a staffing or equipment shortage affecting Ridgewood sanitation routes this week?
Interview DSNY about the spike and whether service interruptions occurred.
